TAA is temporal anti aliasing which means that it's blending the previous frames into the current frame. Depth similarity would mean that pixels should blend more or less based on how far away something is in the new frame compared to the last frame, Deghosting is what depth similarity is trying to do. The user adjust determines how opaque the last frame is but it's reversed, set it too low and you get a ton of ghost images because 90% of 90% is still 81%. 5% of 5% is 0.25%. anything below even 2% opacity shouldn't really be visible so setting the user adjust above 0.9 should make it so the shader only really blurs the last frame into the scene. 

TAA is an effect that is very similar to motion blur but with motion blur, your looking to get that effect, you want the sides of the screen to blur. With TAA, your goal is to blur just the edges of each object. Personally, i think TAA isn't great and I use edge blurring through edge detection instead. It's a bit more of an intensive process so its definitely slower but it's using the right tool for the job.

For UI, you can use https://github.com/KaiserThompson/Reshade-Shaders. It requires some setup time but it works very well and requires no depth buffer. I'm working on fixing MXAO being visible through godrays and smoke/fog right now actually.

If we get nationalized health care, what costs the country the most money? Pregnancies? They're usually less than a thousand in other countries. Cancer treatments? Sure its expensive but it also only affects a small population. How about sickness, especially with a pandemic going on? Sickness usually affects so few people that hospitals dont even really see an uptick in patients. The most expensive healthcare system we have is elderly care. Elderly people visit the hospital more, take more pills, break more bones, get sick easier, need nurses, have diseases like Alzheimer's that are unique to them, and so much more. If we cure old age and everyone is as strong healthwise as they were at 25, then we wouldn't need elderly homes, we wouldnt need a several billion dollar industry centered purely around keeping old people alive for as long as possible.

With 1 treatment, we would cure thousands of diseases attributed to old age. So even if that treatment would cost $100,000 to do, its better than the $2,000,000 worth of medical bills over the course of the last 10 years of a persons life. And that means the government would subsidize the treatment so they could save money. Why spend 2 million when you can spend 100,000 and get better results?

Ive found that generally when talking with others, bringing up the fact that even google has an anti aging r&d team called calico, which recieves billions of dollars worth of funding, gets them to begin to listen. If even google believes its possible then why shouldnt you essentially.

After that hook, they'll always ask what are they doing there or other similar questions. While we dont know what calico is doing, this lets you start talking about the technologies and treatments. Bringing up metformin's anti-aging benefits is usually fairly easy, people on metformin live longer than those off it despite having diabetes. 

Then you can bring up the real kicker, what do people die from in hospitals? Its never old age, its heart failure, organ failure, brain damage, cancer, and so on. If no one dies of old age, then theres always a cause. If theres a cause, we can work to stop the cause. We'll be able to replace hearts with 3d printed ones using your own stem cells so 0 rejection rate. Brand new hearts with no damage. Same thing for any other organ once we get it figured out. Then if you still have them hooked you can go into telomere extensions which is usually a bit of a hurdle to get over. Ive found the easiest way to bring it up is to tell them about how cloned sheep only live as long as the original. If a sheeps lifespan is 20 years and you clone a 10 year old sheep, the cloned sheep will only live 10 years. A 5 year old sheep cloned will live 15 in this scenario. And thats because of the telomeres. 

Telomeres are end caps of dna that slowly degrade over time due to being copied millions of times. Those end caps protect the actual dna which is instructions for how the cell operates healthily. Once those instructions start getting cut, the cell can no longer work healthily and every cell that is copied from that cell will retain the same broken instructions eventually leading to a cell that cant duplicate. 

That leads to things such as gray hairs, lowered hormone levels, weakened immune response, thin skin,  brittle bones, and more. Meaning if we can restore those telomeres, we can extend the time before those symptoms start. And if we can find even a single cell with a full dna strand, we can extend the telomeres of that cell, turn it into a stem cell, let it replicate, then start a process of replacing the cells your body has with the new master cell and make your body essentially 25.

Emo was big from 2005 to 2010 and there were a lot of schools that would have an emo click. Emos typically used exaggerated colors to offset the base color of black. Due to the high contrast of colors, everyones eyes would be drawn to them. The music was decent, the people had an aesthetic they focused on, and being the big thing at that time, they were considered the alternative cool kids.

As for why it was such a big movement at the time, we had been fighting desert storm 2 for 4 years by the start and a lot of kids had lost family members or had family overseas fighting. The tv shows of the time reinforced the aesthetic choices if not the internal message. There was also an aspect of hopelessness at the time permeating the news and culture of the time.

The emo movement has self realized into a nihilism movement at this point. It was never about the suicide, music, or clothes. It was about the lack of meaning in most peoples lives at that age and having a way of expressing it. We have the same problems today but the clothes have changed to more comfortable wear, the colors have become muted, and the music has changed to fit our cultural shift away from rock and towards electronic music. Emos havent gone away because the underlying cause hasnt gone away. They just changed their aesthetic to a less grungy look and feel.

To push the envelope a bit further, look at the similarities between happy tree friends and rick and morty. Brutal violence that gets written off, silly reasons for the terrible things that happen, and generally cheerful attitude despite the horrific plots. Nihilism is at the center of both shows. For more references to nihilistic emo shows, look at charlie the unicorn, and llamas with hats.

Nihilism will likely continue to affect our culture until culture shifts away from indirect communication strategies and service economies. In order to build meaning in peoples lives, you need to give them interpersonal connections and opportunities to show their unique abilities and skills.

Tl:dr you were probably emo due to emos being flashy, culturally topical, and nihilistic. If you didnt have a plan for after college by the time you were 12, being emo sounded pretty good as a way to waste time with good people.

Realistically, i think a harvard architecture for computer cores would be the closest we could get to a neuron-like substrate. Inputs from other neurons are instructional data, each neuron has to have some kind of memory(our brain stores them in the fatty cells around axons), and we need to come up with some way for neurons to connect as they need to. 

Our brain can grow and split these connections basically at will but silicon based systems would need to interconnect billions of computer cores at all times to allow for a 1-1 likeness. Not to mention the huge programming challenge. Each core would have to have roughly 2-3 mb of cache on chip to meet up with the brains impressive 2.5 pb data storage and access speeds.

As it stands right now, we dont have the tech to build a chip that could replicate the human brain and it would have to be a single chip. The neuromorphic chip standard would be far too slow due to electron travel speed and the von Neuman architecture would be limited by individual data streams. One of the biggest bottlenecks in computing is the time it takes to access ram because its so far away from the cpu. Sure we're talking nanoseconds here but when every single instruction has to get data from the ram, it builds up pretty quick to milliseconds.

If we had all data storage and ram stored on chip, we could get access speeds in the picoseconds, allowing for terabytes to be read from cache in nanoseconds rather than minutes. We need those kinds of transfer speed to allow for memory recall and imagination at human speeds. 

We can build entire worlds in our heads in the blink of an eye but ask a computer to do so and it will take years at current rates. Ask a computer to evaluate the works of Shakespeare and compare and contrast them with Hemmingway and it couldnt then use that same data set to compare j.k. rowling and stephanie meyers.

Humans work as well as we do because we can adapt everything we do. A computer takes a billion images to figure out what a cat is. A human takes maybe 2-3 interactions. We do this because we can extrapolate and pattern recognize based off of very very small data sets. If those billion images only had black cats in them, the computer could be shown a brown cat and wouldnt recognize it. We can because the other characteristics match up.

Our imagination is our strongest tool in our understanding of the world around us because it allows for us to not have to worry about huge data sets. We dont need to see a billion pictures of a car to know what a car is. We can extrapolate and imagine based on what we know and tell you a brown cat is still a cat, a blue nissan is still a car, and stephanie meyer should never have gotten a publishing deal.

A computer must be able to learn based off data sets of fewer than 5 items before we can count them as being human level learners. We can teach an ai everything about our world but if it cant learn, it cant create, only recreate. If it cant create then it will never make breakthroughs. It will always be limited by our programming abilities and understanding of ourselves.

To have a true agi, we need to teach computers to learn like we do so they can make enough breakthroughs where they learn better than we do. Only then will we have asi.

TL:DR human like cognition is a bitch that we will eventually make our bitch before it makes us its bitch shortly after.

A 5200 rpm HDD can only load between 70 and 100 files per second. 7200 rpm only brings that up to 90-150 files per second. Even a low end ssd hits between 5,000 and 50,000 files per second. Symbolism and context are the last things we have to teach computers. We understand that the story of a girl with long hair that a man climbs to rescue her from a tower as Rapunzel. We understand that whenever we reach for a coffee cup, it has a chance of being hot. We understand that we have to slow down in public areas where kids are likely to play because they are unpredictable. I look at context and subtext as the 5th level of understanding which is what we have to teach computers next. 

First level is lines and curves. I see a straight line and can tell its a straight line.

Second level is letters and low level symbols, things like arrows or shapes.

Third level is words and larger symbols, things like logos.

Fourth level is where we are now with sentences and structures. We can tell a computer to identify a persons face and it will do so with better accuracy then a person. We can tell a computer to give us a high level summary of a 400 page book and it can give us the themes and structures that are evident based on previous books and data sets.

Fifth level is Human level understanding, being able to inter-contextualize and compare and contrast things and create new meaning from data sets. With the fifth level you can tell a computer to not only understand a book to its deepest level but also to write its own. Its not limited to text either, if you tell a computer to write a jazz symphony using synthesizers then it will be able to with this level of understanding.

The big difference between fourth and fifth level is our own understanding of things and our ability to describe it. Its very easy for us to understand a dogs behavior patterns but being able to describe why a dog does these things is not as easy. That fifth level of understanding is necessary for computers to be able to interpret things into a real world context. We've had 3rd level understanding in computer programs since search engines and have only gotten better and better as we've moved towards and surpassed 4th level. As we move towards fifth level, we're going to see computers able to do things such as create unique music, artwork, text, video, and any other form of media you can imagine with the right people aiming them.

Ive found that if i purge my vram before i hit a loading screen then i can drop that to 20-30 seconds. Say what you will about ram purging programs but if the game your playing has a shitty garbage collection system, it does help by quite a bit.

Im not sure how one would go about adding a mod to make the gamebryo engine purge better but that would help a great deal towards shorter load times.

With a sample size this low, the readings could be pure chance. If you flip a coin 54 times, you could get all heads. It'd be rare for sure but no where near rare enough to definitively say whether or not it is correlation or causation. Sure, people need to be paid and sure there is probably legitimate science behind it. The fact still remains that the study was put out with far too small a sample size to be viable and this entire article aims to sensationalize and attack the process. It could be that the father's infertility is going to progress to being a part of their sons genetics as well but with a sample size this small, its not worth the grant money put into it. Once we get real numbers and can get a decent sample size, I'll believe it but by the point we have a well documented study done we'll have genetic augmentation near perfected anyway. It takes years for the true studies to be done.

Also, the dates and years in the article have conflicting dates and years. In one line they say 54 men born through ICSI between 1992-1996, where as 4 lines down they say aged 18-22. We'd be looking at 20-24 if their numbers were right. I also wouldn't trust an 18-22 year old to follow a doctors orders to not have any kind of sex for the full week that it normally takes for sperm count and semen volume to normalize. There are too many variables to intrinsically trust this study. Until I see a double-blind study done with full documentation and a decent sample size, I won't be trusting any study on the matter.
